rounds.text: Aequs Ltd exhibits strong top-line momentum, driven by compounded sales growth of 15% over 3 years and accelerating to 33% over the trailing twelve months, alongside screening notes highlighting robust year-over-year sales surges of up to 55% [E13, E14, E50, E51]. This commercial expansion is reinforced by operational scaling, as capital-work-in-progress (CWIP) has dropped by 80.0% to Rs 79 Cr, signaling that major capital expenditure is largely completed and new manufacturing capacity is successfully coming online [E30]. Concurrently, management has de-leveraged the balance sheet, reducing total borrowings from Rs 785 Cr to Rs 701 Cr [E29]. Market participants are rewarding this underlying transition; the stock sits strongly near its highs at 87% of its 52-week range, trades comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages in a golden cross formation, and commands an exceptional relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E35, E37, E38]. Furthermore, foreign institutional investors have increased their holdings from 4.05% to 5.17%, while the broader Capital Goods sector enjoys a robust macro tailwind score of +1.04 [E32, E60]. Conceded: [E15, E16, E24, E25, E56].

Aequs Ltd trades at an extreme valuation that is completely disconnected from its underlying fundamental reality, boasting a price-to-book ratio of nearly 11x against a sector benchmark of just 2.52x [E1, E6]. This rich multiple is paired with severe profitability failures, including a trailing twelve month P/E of -95.91x, a negative return on equity of -10%, and a trailing profit growth collapse of -74% [E5, E8, E16]. Cash generation is deeply impaired, underscored by a devastating free cash flow of Rs -440 Cr and negative operating cash flow of Rs -99 Cr in March 2026 [E24, E25]. Furthermore, operating margins have been on a multi-year downward trend, falling 7 percentage points over the last three years to just 6% in the TTM period [E19, E21]. Institutional capital is actively retreating from this profile, reflected by negative institutional money flow and a net decrease in domestic institutional holdings [E33, E34]. Conceded: the company displays strong top-line momentum with compounded sales growth of 33% in the trailing twelve months and benefits from a supportive capital goods sector tailwind [E14, E59].

Conceded: trailing twelve month P/E is -95.91x and trailing profit growth stands at -74% [E5, E16]. However, the bear's focus on historical losses misses the inflection point where top-line acceleration outpaces legacy headwinds, evidenced by 33% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and quarterly sales and profit upticks [E14, E52, E53]. The extreme price-to-book multiple of nearly 11x is justified by heavy structural investment completing in real time, demonstrated by Capital Work in Progress collapsing by 80% to Rs 79 Cr as new capacity comes online [E1, E30]. While operating cash flow was negative at Rs -99 Cr, borrowings were successfully reduced down to Rs 701 Cr from Rs 785 Cr, showing balance sheet de-leveraging during the investment phase [E24, E29]. Conceded: operating margins have compressed to 6% in the TTM and institutional money flow shows negative near-term signals [E19, E34]. Yet foreign institutions increased their stake to 5.17% alongside stable promoter backing at 59.09%, while a relative-strength rating of 100 and a Sharpe ratio of 1.50 confirm market participants are aggressively rewarding the underlying operating momentum within a supportive capital goods tailwind [E31, E32, E38, E41, E59].

Conceded: foreign institutions increased their stake to 5.17% [E32], but overall institutional money flow remains negative with domestic institutions slashing their holdings by 2.78 percentage points [E33, E34]. The claim that top-line acceleration overcomes legacy headwinds ignores that compounded profit growth over 3 years is -5% and has plunged -74% over the trailing twelve months alongside a staggering net profit decline of -1425% YoY [E15, E16, E54]. The argument that an 80% drop in Capital Work in Progress to Rs 79 Cr justifies an 11x price-to-book multiple [E1, E30] is contradicted by severe negative free cash flow of Rs -440 Cr and negative operating cash flow of Rs -99 Cr in March 2026 [E25, E26]. Conceded: borrowings decreased to Rs 701 Cr [E29], yet the company operates with a low interest coverage ratio, rising debtor days from 64.0 to 78.5, and earnings heavily padded by Rs 65.5 Cr in other income [E45, E47, E48]. Finally, leaning on a relative-strength rating of 100 [E38] to excuse fundamentals ignores that operating margins have compressed by 7 percentage points over both the TTM and the latest quarter, locking the yearly margin trend into a 4-year decline [E19, E20, E21].
